de.my_domain.abalone.model

Enum Direction

  • java.lang.Object
    • java.lang.Enum<Direction>
      • de.my_domain.abalone.model.Direction
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    java.io.Serializable, java.lang.Comparable<Direction>

    public enum Direction
extends java.lang.Enum<Direction>
    The Direction Enum. The Direction enum describes direction for the game Abalone. It provides six different directions in which the player is able to move. As well as methods to obtain a element of direction and its offset, which describes the move as an integer in row and diagonal direction.

      • getRowOffset

        public int getRowOffset()
        The getRowOffset method is the getter Method of the variable rowOffset. The rowOffset is the shift in the row coordinate which must be done to move in a certain direction.
        Returns:
        The rowOffset of an Direction enum will be returned.

      • getDiagOffset

        public int getDiagOffset()
        The getDiagOffset method is the getter Method of the variable diagOffset. The diagOffset is the shift in the diag coordinate which must be done to move in a certain direction.
        Returns:
        The diagOffset of an Direction enum will be returned.

      • getMove

        public static Direction getMove(int rowFrom,
                                int diagFrom,
                                int rowTo,
                                int diagTo)
        The getMove method takes initial coordinates and final coordinates of a move and returns a direction representing this move. Hereby it checks if the requested move corresponds to one of the six legal directions. If this is not the case null will be returned.
        Parameters:
        rowFrom - Is the initial row coordinate.
        diagFrom - Is the initial diagonal coordinate.
        rowTo - Is the final row coordinate.
        diagTo - Is the final diag coordinate.
        Returns:
        The direction of the requested move will be returned. If the requested move is illegal null will be returned.
